5e9cb9311f81bf1ad9fcef04d32034119ebd1008.summary: Describes two new Monero cryptocurrency-mining malware attacks, one on Windows PCs and one on Android devices, both disguised as legitimate updates. The Windows infection, reported by Quick Heal Security Labs, unpacks scripts and a mining program, keeps itself persistent, caps mining CPU use at 35 percent and checks for analysis and antivirus tools. The Android malware HiddenMiner, reported by Fortinet, poses as a Google Play Store update, asks for administrator rights and shuts down in emulators. The article notes IBM X-Force Exchange guidance that HiddenMiner does not run on Android 7.0 or…

5e0c595451085d5955884726970a4ce860178bca.summary: A code-hosting repository page advertising a tool that builds a Windows trojan. It describes keylogging, screen capture and remote command control. It is a tool listing, not an analysis of threat activity, so no threat facts are recorded.

5e48fa8ab017554c8a3407eaf6ae01823a4558ff.summary: TrendAI Research describes a cluster of trojanized npm packages, presented as date utilities, that carry a Linux ELF loader. The loader starts the RedShell Linux implant of the RedC2 4.0 framework on module import, without install hooks. RedC2 is marketed on Hack Forums and includes Red Agent, an LLM assistant that turns natural-language commands into framework tasks.
